model: WeatherExpert 48/50N2-N9 Rooftop (ComfortLink 6.x, UPC Open BACnet option)
applies_to: Carrier WeatherExpert 48/50N2 through N9 packaged rooftop units (gas, electric or hydronic heat) with ComfortLink version 6.x controls and the BACnet communication option.
summary: This is the ComfortLink 6.x generation of the WeatherExpert 48/50N. BACnet MS/TP comes from a UPC Open controller in its own enclosure below the main control box, which reads the ComfortLink board over CCN. The list has 351 objects (AVs, BVs and one multistate value): occupancy, supply air and static pressure setpoints, air temperatures, pressures and flows, up to four compressors per circuit, heat, economizer, Motormaster and VFD values, Humidi-MiZer, airside linkage values, thermostat inputs, alarm flags and spare user values.
default_device_instance: Network number 16101 followed by the MAC address (MAC 20 gives 1610120)
notes: Form 48/50N-6T (4-18) for ComfortLink 6.x units. All 164 objects of the ComfortLink 11.x list (48-50N-8T) are also here; this older list adds 187 more, mostly individual alarm flags, linkage values and service data.
Object names end in _1. Descriptions are the printed point descriptions, with the CCN point name added where two rows share a description.

Econ3 Act. Unavailable? is printed as BV60 (no colon) and kept as BV 60. The Linkage Collector row (link_collector_1) prints no object ID and is left out. Cir B Discharge Pressure (AV 1605) is printed twice and kept once.
Air Source Mode is printed as MSV:2005 (mapped as MV 2005).
Units printed as dF are shown as °F; °^F as Δ°F (temperature differences). Ranges and defaults are left out.

source.title: WeatherExpert 48/50N2,N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8,N9 Packaged Rooftop Cooling Units with Gas Heat, Optional Electric Heat, or Hydronic Heat and ComfortLink Controls Version 6.x - Controls, Start-Up, Operation, Service and Troubleshooting (Appendix F: BACnet Communication Option, Network Points List)

integration.summary: The BMS talks BACnet MS/TP to the UPC Open, which reads and writes the ComfortLink control over CCN. Clear Local Machine Disable, set the CCN schedule number for the occupancy source you want, then write occupancy and (for VAV) the supply air and duct static setpoints; read HVAC mode, temperatures, fan speed and alarm state. Values the BMS feeds in are forces that clear if not refreshed.

integration.enable: The unit ships with Local Machine Disable (Service Test > STOP, BV 59 unitstop_1) set to Yes; set it to No before the unit runs. Occupancy follows the ComfortLink CCN schedule number (SCH.N): 0 = always occupied, 1 = local schedule, 65-99 = a CCN schedule. The points list makes Occupied? (BV 2008) writable, but the manual does not describe how a write interacts with SCH.N; test it on site.
integration.heartbeat: The manual says forces at CCN priority 7 clear unless rewritten in time: outside air temperature, outside RH, outside air quality and static pressure reset after 30 minutes, return air and space temperature after 3 minutes.
integration.remote_sensors: Space Temperature (AV 137), Return Air Temperature (AV 135), Outside Air Temperature (AV 1003), Outside Air RH (AV 119), IAQ (AV 1009) and OAQ (AV 113) are writable. Refresh them within the force timeouts (3 min for space and return temperature, 30 min for outdoor values).
setup: Set the MAC address on the UPC Open's Tens and Ones rotary switches; the controller reads switches, DIP switches and jumpers only at power-up.
Device instance = network number (default 16101) followed by the MAC address, e.g. MAC 20 gives 1610120.
BAS port: DS3 enable, DS4 E1-485, DS5-DS8 set to MSTP; baud on DS1-DS2 (9600, 19.2k, 38.4k or 76.8k, Carrier default 76.8k); 8N1 fixed. EIA-485 jumpers to EIA-485 and 2W.
Fit a BT485 terminator on the first and last controller of the MS/TP segment.
The UPC Open and the ComfortLink board must use the same CCN element and bus numbers (factory 1 and 0).
gotchas: Points depend on unit options (heat type, economizer, Humidi-MiZer, VFDs, airflow monitoring, controls expansion boards); objects for options not fitted carry no useful data.
Thermostat inputs (Y1, Y2, W1, W2, G) and switch inputs are writable BVs (CCN forces).
The user-defined analog and binary values are spare objects with no unit function.
